answer: It does. The audit looked at `agy --help` and at Maestro (which has no Antigravity driver). The surface is the status-line payload, and the installed CLI runs a quota manager that force-refreshes it from Google's backend.
consequences_for_maestro: FOUR pools on one account, not one: a Gemini pool and a separate third-party ('3p') pool, each with its own 5-hour and weekly window and its own independent reset. This is the strongest confirmation yet of the composite account_pool_id decision, and it is now a measured fact rather than an adopted schema generality.
The pools diverge sharply in practice — 3p-weekly at 27% remaining while gemini-weekly sat at 90% — so a single per-account headroom number would have been actively wrong.

Quota is expressed as remaining_fraction, not used_pct, and the reset arrives both absolutely (reset_time) and relatively (reset_in_seconds). QuotaObservation must normalise remaining/used and accept either reset form.
The payload also carries plan_tier, model id, context_window used/remaining percentage and token counts, and an agent_state field — an idle/busy signal none of the other backends expose.

Acquisition is the same PUSH pattern as Claude: the payload is delivered to a status-line command, not pulled on demand. Two of three backends therefore depend on a renderer Maestro does not control, which strengthens rather than weakens the acquisition-path finding in b02-quota-acquisition-path.json.
correction_of: GRAPH_ENGINEERING_RESEARCH_BLIND_SPOTS.md B06 row and MAESTRO_GRAPH_ENGINEERING_ARCHITECTURE.html P6 ('agy 1.1.27 exposes no usage surface at all')

evidence.shows: a top-level `quota` object with four independent pools
evidence.source: ~/.gemini/statusline_dump.json (operator capture, product antigravity, CLI version 1.0.10, sampled 2026-06-21)

evidence.shows: quota_manager.go doRefreshQuota: starting reload (force=true) — the installed version actively refreshes quota from the backend
no usage/quota subcommand — which is why the audit's help-only inspection missed it

limits: The pool shape comes from a 1.0.10 capture. The installed 1.1.27 provably still maintains and refreshes quota, but its exact payload was not re-captured — re-capture before an Antigravity adapter is called supported (B06 gate).
Whether the payload can be obtained without an interactive session, and whether a headless `--print` run emits it, was not tested.
No Maestro driver exists for this backend, so nothing consumes any of it yet.
question: Does the installed Antigravity CLI expose a subscription quota surface? The 2026-09-08 audit recorded 'no usage surface observed' and the plan was amended to say routing must tolerate a quota-unavailable backend.
